title: Critical theta-half modular centering and Gibbs variance reduction
question: Can the theta-half Gibbs cancellation be centered in the bond Gibbs state itself, replacing the raw local second moment by a thermal variance without changing the Kubo-Mori shell, and does the finite Q3 stress reveal whether this removes the observed cutoff growth?
promotion_boundary: R-372 proves only a finite algebraic re-centering of the R-371 theta-half shell and checks it on the actual-Q3 edge and square proxies. It does not prove that the bond Gibbs variance is uniformly bounded, nor that the local proxy is the full interacting KMS state.
next_action: Prove or obstruct a source-, volume- and cutoff-uniform thermal-variance estimate on a Hamiltonian-derived common core; only then combine the variance form with the R-370 frequency split for the direct D,delta-D corridor.
boundary: Finite doubled-bond Gibbs proxy, all-prefix actual-Q3 edge and square rows, translated sites and selected bonds, both orientations, signs, adjoints and beta values. Uniform variance, global KMS, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.
